title: Boasting About the Melons You’re Selling
synopsis: What does it mean to “boast about the melons you’re selling”?

fullText.simplified:
王婆卖瓜，自卖自夸

    王婆听起来在说女人，其实他是个男人。他姓王，叫王坡。因为他说话啰啰嗦嗦，做事婆婆妈妈，人们就给他起了个外号——王婆。
    王婆是宋朝人，他的老家好像是在新疆附近，靠种瓜卖瓜生活。那时，宋朝边境总有战争，王婆为了避难，就搬到了河南开封的乡下。他用从新疆带来的哈密瓜种子，继续种瓜卖瓜。当时开封的老百姓没见过哈密瓜。虽然哈密瓜比一般西瓜甜十倍，但是因为样子难看，所以根本没人买。
    王婆心里着急，就开始大声叫卖，向行人推销他的瓜，还把瓜切开让大家尝。一开始没人吃，后来有个胆大的尝了一口，大叫：太甜了。就这样，一传十，十传百，王婆的生意越来越红火。
    一天，宋朝皇帝出宫游玩儿，来到街上，看见一个瓜摊前挤满了人，就问手下人：“那里出了什么事？”。手下人说：“那是个卖瓜的人，他在夸自己的瓜甜。”皇帝觉得有意思，就走到了瓜摊前看王婆卖瓜。王婆看见了皇帝也不害怕，还让皇帝品尝。皇帝吃完问：“你这瓜这么甜，买的人肯定不少，你为什么还大声叫卖呢？”。王婆说：“这边的人没见过这种瓜，不叫卖就没人买了。”
    皇帝听了，说：“对，做买卖该夸的时候就得夸。像王婆卖瓜，自卖自夸，这样也挺好。”皇帝这么一夸，没多久，这句“王婆卖瓜，自卖自夸”就传遍了大江南北，一直用到了今天。
    只不过，现在的“王婆卖瓜，自卖自夸”是贬义，意思是：自己说自己好，但有可能是吹牛，不符合实际。比如：你说了半天，我看是王婆卖瓜，自卖自夸，别人并没有觉得你的产品有多好。再比如：不用让他提建议，他总是喜欢王婆卖瓜，自卖自夸。
    怎么样？你学会了吗？
fullText.traditional:
王婆賣瓜，自賣自誇

    王婆聽起來在說女人，其實他是個男人。他姓王，叫王坡。因為他說話囉囉嗦嗦，做事婆婆媽媽，人們就給他起了個外號——王婆。
    王婆是宋朝人，他的老家好像是在新疆附近，靠種瓜賣瓜生活。那時，宋朝邊境總有戰爭，王婆為了避難，就搬到了河南開封的鄉下。他用從新疆帶來的哈密瓜種子，繼續種瓜賣瓜。當時開封的老百姓沒見過哈密瓜。雖然哈密瓜比一般西瓜甜十倍，但是因為樣子難看，所以根本沒人買。
    王婆心裡著急，就開始大聲叫賣，向行人推銷他的瓜，還把瓜切開讓大家嘗。一開始沒人吃，後來有個膽大的嘗了一口，大叫：太甜了。就這樣，一傳十，十傳百，王婆的生意越來越紅火。
    一天，宋朝皇帝出宮遊玩兒，來到街上，看見一個瓜攤前擠滿了人，就問手下人：“那裡出了什麼事？”。手下人說：“那是個賣瓜的人，他在誇自己的瓜甜。”皇帝覺得有意思，就走到了瓜攤前看王婆賣瓜。王婆看見了皇帝也不害怕，還讓皇帝品嘗。皇帝吃完問：“你這瓜這麼甜，買的人肯定不少，你為什麼還大聲叫賣呢？”。王婆說：“這邊的人沒見過這種瓜，不叫賣就沒人買了。”
    皇帝聽了，說：“對，做買賣該誇的時候就得誇。像王婆賣瓜，自賣自誇，這樣也挺好。”皇帝這麼一誇，沒多久，這句“王婆賣瓜，自賣自誇”就傳遍了大江南北，一直用到了今天。
    只不過，現在的“王婆賣瓜，自賣自誇”是貶義，意思是：自己說自己好，但有可能是吹牛，不符合實際。比如：你說了半天，我看是王婆賣瓜，自賣自誇，別人並沒有覺得你的產品有多好。再比如：不用讓他提建議，他總是喜歡王婆賣瓜，自賣自誇。
    怎麼樣？你學會了嗎？

raw.synopsis: What does it mean to “boast about the melons you’re selling”?
sentence_translations: Granny Wang Boasting About the Melons He’s Selling
Granny Wang’s name sounds like it belongs to a woman, but in fact, he was a man.
His surname was Wang; his full name was Wang Po.
But because he was a bit of a windbag and fussed about everything, people gave him the nickname Granny Wang.
Granny Wang was born during the Song Dynasty.
His hometown was likely somewhere around Xinjiang province, and he earned his living by growing and selling melons.
At that time, during the Song Dynasty, there were always some border conflicts going on.
In order to seek refuge, he moved to the countryside in Kaifeng, Henan province.
He used the cantaloupe seeds that he brought with him from Xinjiang, and continued to grow and sell melons.
At that time, the people of Kaifeng had never seen cantaloupe before.
Though cantaloupe was ten times sweeter than the ordinary watermelon, ..
.. no one wanted to buy them because they had an ugly appearance.
Granny Wang was anxious, so he began to hawk his melons loudly to passersby.
He even cut open the melons for everyone to taste.
At first, no one wanted to try them. Eventually, a brave person took a bite and exclaimed, “It’s so sweet!”
Just like that, one person brought ten people, and those ten people brought a hundred.
Granny Wang’s business began to boom.
One day, the emperor of the Song Dynasty went outside the palace on a tour.
When he came out into the street, he saw many people crowded around a melon stand.
He asked his servant, “What happened there?”
His servant answered, “That’s a melon vendor; he’s boasting about his melons.”
The emperor thought this was interesting, so he walked over to the melon stand to watch Granny Wang sell melons.
Granny Wang wasn’t at all intimidated upon seeing the emperor; he even let the emperor try one of his melons.
After the emperor finished eating, he asked, “These melons are so sweet; there must be a lot of people buying them.
Why do you still hawk them loudly?”
Granny Wang said, “People here have never seen this kind of melon.
If I don’t hawk them loudly, no one will buy them.”
The emperor heard this and replied, “Yes, when doing business, you should boast when you need to boast.
Like Granny Wang boasting about the melons he’s selling. Very good.”
Soon after the emperor praised him like that, ..
.. the phrase “Granny Wang boasting about the melons he’s selling” spread all over the China, ..
.. and is used even until this day.
However, nowadays the expression “Granny Wang boasting about the melons he’s selling” has a negative connotation.
It refers to where someone says they are good at something, ..
.. but they perhaps are just bragging and not in touch with reality.
For example, “You’ve been talking all day. You’re like Granny Wang boasting about the melons he’s selling.
Other people don’t seem to think your product is all that great.”
Here’s another example, “Don’t ask him for suggestions. He’s always like Granny Wang, boasting about the melons he’s selling.”
What do you think? Have you learned how to use this expression?
